info.title: Zenbu account service
info.description: Accounts, sign-in, profiles, and sync for every Zenbu app (ADR 0011). Sign-in is Better Auth's, under /v1/auth; a test holds each of its answers to this contract. Every error is the Error schema.

accessToken.description: A 15-minute access token from GET /v1/auth/token, which takes the session token a sign-in returns. Never the session token itself.

sessionToken.description: The signed session token from a sign-in's `set-auth-token` header. Send it only to /v1/auth.

id.description: The Zenbu user ID. It never changes.

email.description: The account's email. It can't be changed here.

version.description: The profile revision. It goes up by one with each change, and jumps to the time in milliseconds when the service starts on a restored backup; send it back as `baseVersion` to change the profile.

Error.description: Every error. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `message` is for people and may change.

ProfileConflict.description: The profile changed since `baseVersion`. `current` is the profile as it is now.

baseVersion.description: The profile `version` this change was made to. If the profile has changed since, nothing is changed and the answer is a conflict with the current profile.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters once trimmed, with runs of spaces made one and no control characters. Stored in Unicode NFC.

username.description: 3 to 30 letters a to z, digits, or underscores, unique across accounts. It's normalized first (Unicode NFKC, trimmed, lowercased), so `Kana_Fan` is `kana_fan`. `null` removes it.

changes.description: The entities that changed after the cursor, each once, as they are now, including the ones this request changed.

cursor.description: Opaque, and at most 200 characters. Keep it once the changes are applied, and send it next time.

hasMore.description: More changes are waiting: sync again with the new cursor.

MutationResult.description: `applied`: the change is in, at `version`. `conflict`: the entity changed since `baseVersion`, so nothing changed; `current` is it as it is now. `rejected`: the change can never apply as sent; `error.code` says why. A result is final: to try again, send a new mutation with a new ID.

operation.description: The entity as it is now is in `data`.

cursor.description: The `cursor` from the last answer whose changes the client applied. Leave it out, or send null, to start from the beginning.

limit.description: The most journal entries to read this time. Default 100.

mutations.description: Up to 50 changes made on the device, applied in order before the changes are read.

id.description: A client-made ID, unique for each mutation, such as a UUID. Sending the same mutation again under its ID never applies it twice, and gets the same outcome: applied at the same version, a conflict with the entity as it is then, or a rejection with the same `error.code`. Reusing an ID for a different mutation is rejected with `mutation_id_reused`.

entity.description: The entity type. Only `profile` today; any other is rejected.

entityId.description: For `profile`, the account's ID, or left out.

baseVersion.description: The profile `version` this change was made to. If the profile has changed since, nothing is changed and the answer is a conflict with the current profile.

fields.description: For a `profile` update, `name`, `username`, or both, as in PATCH /v1/me. Each value is a string, number, boolean, or null.

token.description: The session's bare token. Keep the signed one from the `set-auth-token` header instead: it is the refresh token.

SignedInUser.description: Who signed in. GET /v1/me has the profile, with the username and version.

token.description: The ID token Sign in with Apple or Google gave the device.

nonce.description: The nonce from POST /v1/auth/sign-in/nonce, passed to Apple or Google.

token.description: The session's bare token, which names it to POST /v1/auth/revoke-session. It signs nothing in: only the signed one in `set-auth-token` does.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no access token, or one that is expired, forged, or for an account that no longer exists. Get a new one from GET /v1/auth/token.

429.description: `too_many_requests`: this account sent more than 60 requests here in the current minute. Wait the seconds `Retry-After` says.

500.description: `internal`: the service failed, and nothing says why. Try again later, backing off. In a sync, the mutations before the failure stand, and sending the request again answers them as before.

patch.summary: Change the signed-in account's name or username
patch.description: Optimistic concurrency: send the `version` last seen as `baseVersion`. The change goes through only if the profile is still at that version, and then its version goes up by one and it appears in /v1/sync. Sending the current values again changes nothing.

400.description: `bad_request`, or `invalid_fields`: a name or username out of bounds.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no access token, or one that is expired, forged, or for an account that no longer exists. Get a new one from GET /v1/auth/token.

409.description: `version_conflict`, with `current`: the profile changed since `baseVersion`. `username_taken`: another account has that username.

429.description: `too_many_requests`: this account sent more than 60 requests here in the current minute. Wait the seconds `Retry-After` says.

500.description: `internal`: the service failed, and nothing says why. Try again later, backing off. In a sync, the mutations before the failure stand, and sending the request again answers them as before.

post.summary: Send the changes made on the device, and get the changes made elsewhere
post.description: Applies `mutations` in order, then answers with the changes after `cursor`. Every mutation is idempotent by its ID, so a request can be sent again after a lost answer. Each answer holds at most `limit` journal entries; while `hasMore` is true, sync again with the new cursor. Results and changes are bounded by the request limits.

400.description: `bad_request`: the body is not JSON, or not this shape.

401.description: `unauthorized`: no access token, or one that is expired, forged, or for an account that no longer exists. Get a new one from GET /v1/auth/token.

410.description: `invalid_cursor`: the cursor isn't one this service gave this account, or is past what it holds, as after a restore. Nothing was applied. Sync again with no cursor, and keep what comes back.

429.description: `too_many_requests`: this account sent more than 120 requests here in the current minute. Wait the seconds `Retry-After` says.

500.description: `internal`: the service failed, and nothing says why. Try again later, backing off. In a sync, the mutations before the failure stand, and sending the request again answers them as before.

post.description: Answers the same whether or not the email has an account. Five codes per address in 10 minutes.

503.description: `email_unavailable`: no email sender is set up.

post.summary: Sign in with the emailed code
post.description: Makes the account on the first sign-in. A `name` is used only then, held to the profile's name rule.

set-auth-token.description: The signed session token: the refresh token, good for 60 days from its last use. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer` to GET /v1/auth/token for an access token.

403.description: `account_not_linked`: an Apple or Google account has this email; sign in that way, then add the email.

post.summary: A nonce for one Apple or Google sign-in

200.description: Pass `nonce` to Apple or Google; it works once, within `expiresIn` seconds.

post.summary: Sign in with Apple or Google
post.description: With `idToken`, signs in with the token the device got, and makes the account on the first sign-in. Without it, starts the web sign-in, which comes back to GET /v1/auth/callback/{id}. A new account's email must be verified by the provider, and an email that already has an account is refused until the learner adds this way while signed in.

200.description: Signed in, or, without `idToken`, the provider page to send the browser to.

set-auth-token.description: The signed session token: the refresh token, good for 60 days from its last use. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer` to GET /v1/auth/token for an access token.

400.description: `nonce_required`, or a token that is invalid.

409.description: `oauth_link_error`: that email has an account; add this way while signed in.

get.summary: Where Apple's or Google's web sign-in comes back

302.description: On to the `callbackURL` the sign-in started with.

post.summary: Add Apple or Google as another way to sign in
post.description: Needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes. The account email is told.

post.summary: Remove a way to sign in
post.description: Needs a sign-in from the last 10 minutes. The last way never goes. The account's email is told.

accountId.description: The way in's `id` from GET /v1/auth/list-accounts, not its provider's subject.

get.summary: A 15-minute access token for /v1/me, /v1/sync, and the other services

200.description: An EdDSA JWT naming only the account (`sub`).

401.description: `unauthorized`: the session is gone; sign in again.

get.summary: The keys an access token is checked with

200.description: The session, or `null` with no valid one.
